rulebook.title: IGFA International Angling Rules (records and most sport-fishing tournaments)
rulebook.text_used: written from general knowledge of the IGFA rules; igfa.org was not reachable from this session, so the wording was not re-checked. References are section names (the IGFA rules are not numbered like a sports rulebook). Recreational fishing has no referee: these rules decide whether a catch counts.

rod_tip_min_m.note: 40 in, measured from the point directly under the centre of the reel to the tip

rod_butt_max_m.note: 27 in, from under the centre of the reel to the end of the butt; a curved butt is measured in a straight line

equipment.rule: Equipment Regulations, Rods (tip at least 101.6 cm)
Equipment Regulations, Rods (butt at most 68.6 cm)

scene.text: One angler per rod: from the strike until the fish is landed or released, only the angler touches the rod, reel and line.
Fishing from a boat: helpers may take hold of the leader near the boat and gaff or net the fish, but never touch the rod, reel or main line.
Hand-cranked reel only; no electric, hydraulic or motor-driven reel.

scene.rule: Equipment Regulations, Harnesses and rod belts
scene.text: A rod belt (gimbal) or harness may take the butt; the rod does not rest on the gunwale, a rod holder or anything else while the fish is played.

fouls.rule: Angling Regulations; Acts that disqualify a catch
fouls.title: Angler fights the fish alone
fouls.text: The angler must hook, fight and land or boat the fish without the aid of any other person; anyone else touching the rod, reel or line during the fight disqualifies the catch.
fouls.legal: the angler's own hands hold the rod and turn the reel

fouls.title: Rod resting on an object
fouls.text: Resting the rod in a rod holder, on the gunwale or on any other object while playing the fish disqualifies the catch; the butt may sit in a rod belt or harness on the angler's body.
fouls.legal: the rod butt is tucked against the angler's own belly
avoid: rod left in a rod holder during the fight

fouls.title: Handlining
fouls.text: Holding or lifting the fish with the line in the hand, or with a rope tied to the line or leader, disqualifies the catch; the fish is brought in with the rod and reel.
avoid: angler pulling the fishing line by hand

fouls.title: One line on the fish
fouls.text: A fish hooked by more than one line does not count; one angler, one rod, one line.
avoid: two fishing lines from one rod
several rods tangled on one fish

fouls.title: Power-driven reel
fouls.text: Power-driven reels of any kind (electric, hydraulic or motor-driven) are prohibited; the angler cranks the reel by hand.
avoid: electric reel with a power cable
